content:
Good afternoon!
I want to try out LLM's theorem-proving capabilities in Lean.
Please tell me if there's an agent for Lean that can prove theorems. Regular neural networks can't handle tactics well, since the code containing the tactics contains virtually no information about what the tactic is proving. I need access to the interactive Lean debugger. Is there an agent that can view the results of applying tactics?

Claude, in an appropriate IDE or MVP setup, can do this adequately; there are open source models made for this too, like Lean steak; but I would suggest Aristotle as (in my biased opinion :slight_smile:) the strongest and easiest to try: https://aristotle.harmonic.fun/
I can also recommend Codex. For my style of usage, codex is perfectly adequate. I never ask AI to write definitions and theorem statements.
Are there any solutions for VS Code? After all, it's the primary IDE for Lean. Although I certainly like Zed better. Do you think there's any hope that Lean support will appear in Zed this year?
The Lean extension for VS Code is only 21,000 lines of TypeScript.
Claude code has an official vscode plugin. Not sure about codex.

Filipp said:

Are there any solutions for VS Code? After all, it's the primary IDE for Lean. Although I certainly like Zed better. Do you think there's any hope that Lean support will appear in Zed this year?

There is a third party extension by someone. But I am not sure about officially support, probably at some point if Lean becomes more mainstream popular.
The zed extension supports syntax highlighting, but doesn't provide an infoview
There are lean4 skills and a lean lsp server available for both Codex and Claude. lean4 Claude skills are at cameronfreer/lean4-skills
